rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should test a foundational multimodal configuration to establish baseline performance. This experiment tests combining RNA (pca_n2000) and image (resnet50) data with simple concatenation fusion, which clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines. It directly addresses the most critical design choice (multimodal vs single-modality) with minimal complexity, providing maximal information about the potential value of integrating multiple data types.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, concat fusion) achieves 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method to 'weighted' improves performance, clarifying the impact of fusion strategy. It is the best next step as it directly extends the previous configuration to explore a key design choice (fusion method) that could significantly affect performance, balancing exploitation of the multimodal direction with exploration of critical components.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile with concat fusion (config_016) outperforms weighted fusion (config_017). This experiment tests whether multiprofile (a key design choice) improves performance when using the same RNA/image encoders and concat fusion. It clarifies if profile setting is critical, balancing exploration of a new setting with reuse of proven components.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, avgpool aggregation, and concat fusion (config_018) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.6186). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced architecture) while keeping other parameters identical. This clarifies whether the image encoder choice significantly impacts performance, a critical design decision. It balances exploitation (building on the successful config_018) and exploration (testing a stronger image encoder).

Existing evidence shows that using 'imagenet_vit_l' as the image encoder with 'avgpool' aggregation and 'concat' fusion (config_024) achieves high validation accuracy (0.6287). This experiment tests whether switching to 'weighted' fusion (config_025) could further improve performance, clarifying the impact of fusion strategies. It is a logical extension of the promising multimodal multiprofile setup, balancing exploitation of existing high-performance configurations with exploration of critical design choices.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile setups with imagenet_vit_l and weighted fusion (e.g., config_025) achieve the highest accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated model) maintains or improves performance, clarifying the importance of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation (building on the successful multiprofile/weighted fusion pattern) and exploration (testing a new RNA encoder).

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests transformer aggregation (a novel component in this setup) to determine if it further improves performance, leveraging the strong foundation of the current top performer while exploring a key design choice.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve the highest accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 (used in config_039) with scgpt, while keeping the aggregation and fusion strategy the same, could further improve performance. This clarifies the importance of RNA encoder choice in the top-performing architecture, leveraging strong evidence from config_039 while exploring a new encoder variant.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_039) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing scvi_n200 with pca_n2000 RNA encoder while keeping other components the same clarifies the importance of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploration of critical design decisions (RNA encoder) with exploitation of proven effective components (imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted fusion).

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and transformer aggregation achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_039: 0.724989). This experiment tests whether using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with avgpool aggregation in a rna_only setting (config_005) can match or exceed this performance, clarifying if the RNA encoder type or aggregation method is more critical. It balances exploration of RNA-only models with the need to validate key components from high-performing multimodal configurations.
